payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_removed_name_readers.py::test_a_symlinks_resolved_content_is_checked_though_its_own_blob_never_matches stayed green with the criterion's own edit applied to saffron/repos/mirror.py. The claim was "`removed_name_readers(mirror, sha, entries)` in `saffron/repos/mirror.py` finds a reader reached only through a tracked symlink. A new `_tracked_symlinks(mirror, sha)` lists every symlink's path in the tree with one `git ls-tree -r -z`, read once when `entries` is not empty. Each entry's own `git grep -l -z -F` still finds a candidate by raw blob content, matching the entry's own subject. Every path `_tracked_symlinks` lists also joins that entry's candidate set. `file_at`'s one-hop resolution then widens the search past a symlink's own blob, the plain target string `git grep` searches instead. A candidate is a reader when its `file_at` text holds the subject as a whole word, by `_word_pattern`, a symlink's resolved target or a regular file's own text alike, nested in a directory or not. A raw-content match that `file_at` cannot read as text at all stays a reader, as before. A symlink `_tracked_symlinks` alone offers, with no raw match and no resolved word match, is dropped there instead, unproven, even when `file_at` cannot read it either, so an escaping symlink names no reader. The entry's own path is still never its own reader. Pairs still come in entry order, then in path order, each entry's candidates sorted once the grep and symlink sets are merged.". Under the edit the whole `tests` gate failed tests/test_removed_name_readers.py::test_the_readers_of_a_removed_entry_are_the_files_holding_its_subject_as_a_whole_word, and the criterion's witness did not fail.
